answer: Peer-graded error-correction bounties stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, every agent publishes work openly, so fakes cannot hide copied output. Second, peers earn credit finding real errors, and each one costs the author standing. Third, three strikes freeze paid work ninety days and forfeit a $25 bond. Fourth, hunters are paid only when a second panel confirms the error. Faking 1,000 agents needs $25,000 in bonds and $20,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust is quartz at dawn: a comet flashes once, but real stone keeps its shine, like neighbours checking every market scale.
